name: Elegance and Insight Rubric v4
description: Four sub-criteria rated H/M/L with hard caps, worked examples at all five score levels, anti-patterns section. Pruned from v3's 6 criteria; retained v2's FEWSHOT+ approach plus clearer ANCHOR for 0.75/1.0 boundary.

criteria.name: SC-A: Conceptual Core
criteria.description: Names the structural reason WHY the result holds (not just the technique used).
checks: Points to a key structural fact that immediately entails the result?
Or just names a technique without explaining why it delivers the answer?
Or applies an algorithm without any mechanism?

criteria.name: SC-B: Economy of Means
criteria.description: Insight delivered compactly; core idea fits in 1-3 key sentences.
checks: Could the key point be stated in 1-3 sentences?
Or is it a long chain of manipulation where a shorter path exists?

criteria.name: SC-C: Explanatory Force
criteria.description: Explains WHY transferably; student gains a reusable principle.
checks: After reading, can a student solve a similar problem without re-deriving?
Is the mechanism named, not just the steps?
Or is it purely procedural with local step justifications only?

criteria.name: SC-D: Avoidance of Brute Force
criteria.description: Takes principled route over case enumeration or computer assistance.
checks: Does it avoid computer search, code, or exhaustive case analysis?
Does it take the conceptual path when one is available?

aggregation: Count H scores: 4H=1.0, 3H=0.75, 2H=0.5, 1H=0.25, 0H=0.0. Apply hard caps first.

scores.1.0: 4H: avoids computation, names general principle, all sub-criteria satisfied
scores.0.75: 3H: strong insight on core+economy+force but one sub-criterion M
scores.0.5: 2H: clever first move that resolves into algebra; partial insight
scores.0.25: 1H: correct and organized but purely procedural; HOW not WHY
scores.0.0: 0H: bare result, link, or wall of computation with no mechanism

worked_examples.summary: Bare link to textbook, no mathematical content
I-E counting walkthrough: names technique but not WHY it works
Substitution limit: clever pivot but resolved by algebraic expansion
Lower-triangular: single observation bypasses all computation
Parity uniqueness factorization: WHY is clearly stated, 3 lines
